summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of MSSA bacteremia and C. difficile infection was admitted for a recurrent gastroparesis flare characterized by nausea, vomiting, and abdominal discomfort. Her symptoms were likely triggered by severe hyperglycemia and significant fluid overload, with labs showing glucose of 699 and hyponatremia (Na 123). She was managed with bowel rest, insulin therapy, and two hemodialysis sessions for fluid removal, which led to marked improvement in symptoms and electrolyte balance. Her blood cultures remained negative, and her MSSA bacteremia prophylaxis with cefazolin and vancomycin locks was continued. She completed her metronidazole course for C. difficile and was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating a full diet, with instructions to maintain strict fluid restriction and continue outpatient antibiotic and diabetes management.
